_staleness_note: ref_date drives price staleness on positive legs only (drift > +30% → STALE −3; drift < −15% → DISLOCATED flag, no points; trims and exits are never adjusted; CHECK: possible split only when FMP records a split after ref_date) and expiry at two or more quarter-ends (UNREFRESHED), clocked from `confirmed` — the latest filing still showing the position — when present and is set ONLY on manager and strategic (13F) signals — the period end of the filing where the move happened (Q3→2026-09-30, Q2→2026-06-30). Every manager/strategic signal carries a `trace` to its holdings/ row; exits trace to the prior-quarter row and its absence in the next. Insider signals are sell-side warnings and are intentionally EXEMPT (no ref_date). Price/earnings/screen/senate are events and are also exempt. Do not add ref_date to those lanes.
_rubric: Inspo v4 as applied Nov 24 — NEW: ≥5% of book 9 · 3–5% 7 · 2–3% 6 · 1–2% 4. ADD (by share count): +10–30% → 3 · +30–100% → 4 · >+100% → 5, +1 if the position is ≥5% of book (max 6). HOLD (<10% share change) scores only for a top-3 holding: 3. TRIM: −10–30% → −2 · −30–60% → −3 · beyond −60% → −5. EXIT by prior weight: ≥5% → −7 · 2–5% → −5 · 1–2% → −3 · <1% → −2. Legs are taken only for positions ≥1% of book in either quarter (AMD at Duquesne included by request). Options rows are scored as their own legs; SMH puts at Altimeter are a hedge, hand-set to −3. BASKET: Duquesne's three equal-sized gold miners (NEM, B, AEM) are one signal scored as a 2–3% new position. NEWLY VISIBLE: pre-IPO stakes that became reportable on listing (SpaceX at D1 and NVDA Corp) score 0 — visibility is not a purchase.

changed.p: Split out of AI Compute. META was bought by four managers at once: Whale Rock nearly quadrupled it into its #1 holding, Altimeter added 25%, Light Street opened at 5.9% and SRS added 24%. GOOGL went the other way, cut or sold by Whale Rock, Duquesne and Light Street.
Whale Rock's Q3 rotation: new HPE, VICR, MPWR and SMTC, and adds to SITM, TTMI and VIAV. D1 also nearly tripled MPWR. Almost entirely one manager — see the Step 2 leg cap.

Whale Rock cut SNDK 65% from its #1 spot and sold WDC; Duquesne sold SNDK but built Seagate into its #2 position with calls on top. SRS opened SK Hynix at 4.4%. Druckenmiller's Q1 legs (SNDK, CLS, ARM, MU) are all gone — CLS and MU were sold by June 30.
Whale Rock sold AEIS and TSEM in Q2 and cut LRCX 80% in Q3. Altimeter sold AMAT, KLAC and LRCX outright. Of the Q1 trio, only MKSI is still held, without adds.

Brazil is gone: Duquesne's EWZ calls — the whole signal — were closed by Sep 30. TEVA, ARGT and AXON are sold. Light Street's TEAM, AMPL and CEG were gone before Q2. Altimeter's ARM is still held (4.5%) but no longer moving. Senate, insider, screen and earnings events older than two quarters are retired.
